Explanation

Your application has hardcoded URLs that might correspond to services that are not accessible on Azure.

Review and ensure that the application is attempting to access URLs that would be available from Azure. You might need to migrate those services to Azure too, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.

If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premises, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
SQL database connection detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

SQL database connection detected.

Ensure the database is available/reachable on Azure.

If it is not, there are multiple ways you can move your data to Azure:
1. Migrate to Azure SQL Database.
2. Consider Azure SQL Managed Instance if you need features that are not available in Azure SQL Database and you don’t want to use a VM.
3. Migrate your database servers directly to SQL Server on Azure VMs.

To assess database migration effort, you can use Azure Migrate tool, see the link below.
Local or network IO operations detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 57

Explanation

Your application has local or network IO operations.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, move persistent I/O to storage mounts (Azure Files/UNC). Keep local writes to temp only; connect to external dependencies via private endpoints/VNet to reduce latency.

IO operations outside of the application folder might not be available on Azure App Service. Review and ensure IO APIs are attempting to access paths that will be available when your app is running on App Service sandbox. If you choose the containerized hosting option, your scenario still might be broken or have scalability issues.

Possible solutions:
1. Files that the application needs can be deployed with the application or put in Azure Storage. You can use Azure Storage File Shares as a drop-in replacement for on-premises file share.
2. Other services that the application depends on might need to be migrated to Azure, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.
3. If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premise, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local OS environment access detected
 Potential 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 56

Explanation

Local OS environment access detected.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, Read config via App Settings or App Configuration; avoid machine‑specific environment APIs. Persist environment setup via install scripts when needed.

When running in Azure App Service environment, your application can read environment variables that you define in App Service settings. Using environment API other than reading environment variables might indicate that your application depends on some local machine's features and might be broken on App Service sandbox or not scale well. Review your scenarios and either refactor them to be more cloud friendly or choose the option in App Service to host your application in the sandbox for Windows Container Web Apps.

If you choose to use other Azure hosting options such as Azure Container Apps (ACA) or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), environment APIs might work, however scaling still might be an issue.
Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj
src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj

Explanation

Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, validate on .NET Framework 4.8 or move to .NET 10. Persist any runtime prerequisites via install scripts; test in staging before production.

While if targeting other Azure compute services:

Application targeting .NET framework lower than 4.7.1 might missing features that would be needed for some cloud scenarios like scaling or getting secrets from secure external sources.

Azure App Service runs apps on .NET Framework 4.8 or .NET Framework 3.5. Apps running on on .NET Framework versions older than .NET Framework 4.8 could have potential compatibility issues. It is recommended to test your application running on .NET Framework 4.8. Note that it is not necessary to re-target to .NET Framework 4.8, only to validate that the app correctly runs on that version of .NET Framework.

In the long term it is also recommended to upgrade your application to latest supported .NET 8+ which would significantly increase performance of your application. Use tools like .NET Upgrade Assistant to help with upgrading your application to newer .NET.
Connection strings without configuration builders detected
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

Connection strings without configuration builders detected.

Keeping connection strings directly in the app is not the best practice and might introduce security risks, increased maintenance, scalability challenges or compliance standards (such as PCI DSS, GDPR, etc.).

Instead, it is recommended to use configuration builders to get secrets from secure sources in Azure environment.
System.Data.SqlClient dependency detected
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

System.Data.SqlClient dependency is detected.

While System.Data.SqlClient will work in Azure, the newer Microsoft.Data.SqlClient package is the primary .NET SQL client moving forward and receiving the latest features. For example, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient easily allows use of Azure Managed Identity from a connection string.

Explanation

Static content detected.

Your current approach of serving static content directly might lead to increased costs, performance issues, maintenance challenges (requiring application redeployment for content changes), and security risks.

Consider moving static content to Azure Blob Storage and adding Azure CDN.

WCF Client APIs
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

WCF client-side APIs for building service clients that communicate with WCF services. These APIs are available as exact equivalents via NuGet packages - add System.ServiceModel.* NuGet packages (System.ServiceModel.Http, System.ServiceModel.Primitives, System.ServiceModel.NetTcp, etc.)
Legacy Configuration System
 Mandatory 2
FilePosition

Explanation

Legacy XML-based configuration system (app.config/web.config) that has been replaced by a more flexible configuration model in .NET Core. The old system was rigid and XML-based. Migrate to Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration with JSON/environment variables; use System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager NuGet package as interim bridge if needed.
GDI+ / System.Drawing
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

System.Drawing APIs for 2D graphics, imaging, and printing that are available via NuGet package System.Drawing.Common. Note: Not recommended for server scenarios due to Windows dependencies; consider cross-platform alternatives like SkiaSharp or ImageSharp for new code.
Windows Forms Legacy Controls
 Mandatory 3
FilePosition

Explanation

Legacy Windows Forms controls that have been removed from .NET Core/5+ including StatusBar, DataGrid, ContextMenu, MainMenu, MenuItem, and ToolBar. These controls were replaced by more modern alternatives. Use ToolStrip, MenuStrip, ContextMenuStrip, and DataGridView instead.
Windows Forms
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

Windows Forms APIs for building Windows desktop applications with traditional Forms-based UI that are available in .NET on Windows. Enable Windows Desktop support: Option 1 (Recommended): Target net9.0-windows; Option 2: Add <UseWindowsDesktop>true</UseWindowsDesktop>; Option 3 (Legacy): Use Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop SDK.

Explanation

CVE-2024-21907: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions in Newtonsoft.Json

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependencies:
- Newtonsoft.Json:6.0.4 (declared at src\eShopWinForms\packages.config:5; project assembly reference at src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:63 and package HintPath at src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:64).

Affected range: < 13.0.1. Highly nested JSON can cause stack overflow or excessive CPU/memory consumption, resulting in denial of service. This is a dependency-version finding; application exploitability was not tested.

Recommended fix:
- Upgrade Newtonsoft.Json to 13.0.1 or later after compatibility review. No dependency versions or application files were changed.

Assessment coverage and limitations:
- Required dotnet list package --include-transitive --format json exited 1 because Microsoft.WebApplication.targets was unavailable.
- Fallback inspected both packages.config files and both project files, including PackageReference, assembly Reference/HintPath and ProjectReference declarations. The three distinct detected NuGet coordinates were EntityFramework:6.1.3, Microsoft.AspNet.WebApi.Client:5.2.3 and Newtonsoft.Json:6.0.4. Manifest versions were corroborated with package HintPaths; assembly identity versions were not mistaken for NuGet versions. No PackageReference or ProjectReference declarations were found.
- All three installed-version declarations were checked with the runtime advisory tool and the paginated public GitHub Advisories API (ecosystem nuget). No active advisories were returned for EntityFramework:6.1.3 or Microsoft.AspNet.WebApi.Client:5.2.3. Withdrawn duplicate GHSA-8rfx-6mr3-5jh3 was excluded.
- packages.config is a flat installed-package list and does not reliably distinguish direct from transitive packages. Resolved transitive dependency graph completeness could not be verified; undeclared dependencies and .NET Framework/platform vulnerabilities are outside this NuGet assessment. No restore, build, tests or linters were run.

Data Storage & External Services

The service owns one SQL database, defaulting to LocalDB eShopDatabase; an environment-supplied connection string can replace it (src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\CatalogConfiguration.cs:10-18). Catalog images are read from a working-directory-relative local asset folder, not downloaded from the service (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:48-61). No active cache, message broker, remote identity provider or other external business integration was found in the entry point, controller or hosted service.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The desktop controller composes service responses and drives a view interface; dependencies are manually wired, without a DI container (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:14-20,75-85).
  • Business operations access EntityModel directly; there is no separate repository layer. Missing-database creation and seeding are registered in the context constructor (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:16-25; src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:12-22).
  • Active versus unused: the active client is the generated proxy under Connected Services. The service-side CatalogServiceClient.cs is absent from the service project's explicit compile list; WinForms Helpers files are likewise excluded. CatalogServiceMock is compiled but not selected by either startup or .svc activation; its discount operation throws (src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj:79-94; src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:89-103,109-113,155-159; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogServiceMock.cs:118-120).

API & Service Communication Contracts

Within eShopLegacyNTier, one SOAP service exposes ten request/reply operations at a shared service address. The desktop uses synchronous generated-proxy calls; there are no REST resource routes in the active implementation (src\eShopWCFService\ICatalogService.cs:12-34; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-84).

All rows use the same configured address, http://localhost:62314/CatalogService.svc, with SOAP 1.1 document/literal messages over HTTP POST. SOAP actions follow http://tempuri.org/ICatalogService/ with corresponding response actions. There is no explicit API-version scheme, custom FaultContract, REST-style status model or per-operation HTTP success code declaration. SOAP faults, not invented HTTP 400 contracts, represent service errors.

The current UI invokes classification lists, filtered items, discounts and stock operations. Find/create/update/delete catalog-item operations are exposed but not invoked by its controller (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-157). The generated GetCatalogItems(int?, int?) and checked-in XSD's nillable filter elements differ from the current service's non-nullable parameters: callers here pass concrete integers, but nullable wire-contract compatibility requires verification rather than assuming generated metadata is current (src\eShopWinForms\Connected Services\eShopServiceReference\CatalogService.xsd:31-35).

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogType and DiscountItem are mutable service-level response contracts; CatalogItem is also the create/update/remove request contract. CatalogItemsStock is a mutable stock-update request contract. Entities are directly annotated with DataContract and DataMember and reused as persistence models, not immutable records or gateway composition DTOs (src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItem.cs:10-35; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogBrand.cs:10-19; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogType.cs:10-19; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItemsStock.cs:10-25; src\eShopWCFService\Models\DiscountItem.cs:11-31).

WCF data-contract XML serialization is the active protocol. Generated mutable client copies implement property-change notifications; generated Task-based alternatives are client convenience methods, not separate asynchronous message-based services (src\eShopWinForms\Connected Services\eShopServiceReference\Reference.cs:461-505). WSDL/XSD files are checked in beside the proxy; no OpenAPI, protobuf or GraphQL contract is present in the scoped project declarations (src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:122-134). See data-architecture.md for fields and relationships.

Communication Patterns

  • Synchronous: UI events call a controller, which uses a generated WCF proxy; the service executes EF queries and saves synchronously. Catalog and discount responses are combined in the desktop display, not in an API gateway (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:75-85; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-117).
  • No asynchronous integration: no queue, event bus, background scheduler, service discovery, load-balancer or gateway implementation was found in the active paths. The endpoint is a configured localhost address.
  • Resilience: no retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead, fallback or application-configured binding timeout values are present. The empty binding uses WCF framework defaults; numeric timeout settings are not explicitly declared (src\eShopWinForms\App.config:20-28). The controller has no exception-handling path; service outages are not converted into empty results. A missing stock row returns zero and a missing discount returns null, which are domain results rather than outage fallbacks (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-30,90-96).
  • Startup: the service and its database must be available before the desktop's initial data calls; the dialog is shown only after LoadView. No readiness orchestration is declared; see configuration-inventory.md (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27).
  • Security posture: the selected basicHttpBinding client/server route is plain HTTP, with no explicit binding security override, supplied client credentials, service authorization checks or authentication logic in the inspected active code/config. A separate HTTPS protocol mapping and HTTPS metadata switch do not secure the explicitly configured HTTP route. Actual IIS/network access restrictions cannot be determined from source (src\eShopWCFService\Web.config:22-42; src\eShopWinForms\App.config:19-28; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:14-117).
  • Unused alternatives: the service-folder hand-written CatalogServiceClient.cs is excluded from compilation and must not be mistaken for the active generated proxy. The compiled mock is not activated and its unimplemented discount behavior is not the active service behavior (src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj:79-94; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc:1; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogServiceMock.cs:118-120).

Core Business Workflows

eShopLegacyNTier lets users browse merchandise by brand/type, see current promotional pricing, inspect stock for a chosen date, and record shipment availability. It does not implement shopping carts, ordering, payment, checkout or customer accounts in the inspected active code.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogService / catalog managementMerchandise shown in the catalogClassified by brand and type; referenced by dated inventory
CatalogBrandCatalogService / catalog classificationProduct brand used to filter merchandiseGroups catalog items
CatalogTypeCatalogService / catalog classificationProduct category used to filter merchandiseGroups catalog items
CatalogItemsStockCatalogService / inventory availabilityRecorded quantity for one item on a calendar dateLogical reference to merchandise; no separate shipment aggregate
DiscountItemCatalogService / promotionsStorewide fractional discount valid for a date intervalApplied to displayed catalog prices; not linked to specific merchandise

Evidence: src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItem.cs:10-35; Models\CatalogBrand.cs:10-19; Models\CatalogType.cs:10-19; Models\CatalogItemsStock.cs:10-25; Models\DiscountItem.cs:11-31; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-30,90-117. These are functional groupings inside one service, not separately implemented DDD bounded-context services.

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
CatalogService / eShopWCFServiceCatalog, classification, promotions and inventoryAll five domain entitiesOne database through EntityModel; seed factories for initial sample records
eShopWinForms / CatalogControllerCatalog browsing and stock-maintenance user interactionNo authoritative persistent entities; generated contract copiesCatalogService SOAP operations; local catalog image assets

The service is the source of truth; the desktop composes display data without owning another domain store. No independent order/customer domain exchange is implemented (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:18-22; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-84; src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:55-61).

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse and filter catalog with current promotional pricing

  1. Startup wires the controller and view, checks the current promotion, loads catalog items and classification filters, then populates inventory-selection lists before displaying the window (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:150-157).
  2. The controller adds an All choice to both classification lists. Changing either selection raises a filter event carrying both selections (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:98-143; src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:106-135).
  3. The controller clears the grid, retrieves matching items and separately asks for today's discount. The service uses the All-filter rule and Active-promotion rule below (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:75-85; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-30,56-62).
  4. The view computes Promotional display price, reads product images locally and adds rows. With no active discount, it displays base prices. The initial banner is separate from price loading and is not refreshed by later filter changes (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:48-61; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:60-84).

There is no purchase or inventory reservation side effect. A transport/database/image-loading failure has no implemented graceful degradation path.

Workflow 2: Inspect dated stock availability

  1. The user selects an item and calendar date. The view extracts the item identifier from the selection text and raises a stock-search event (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:142-151).
  2. The controller requests that item/day's stock. The service applies the Dated-stock lookup rule, returning zero if no row matches (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:50-54; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:90-96).
  3. The result is appended to the displayed stock history; it is not accumulated across earlier dates or treated as a reservation (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:173-182).

The search handler does not guard a missing selected item. Zero inventory is a business result, not a service-outage fallback.

Workflow 3: Record or replace shipment availability

  1. The user supplies an item, quantity and arrival date. The view applies Shipment-entry presence/parsing checks and raises an event (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:157-167).
  2. The controller creates a stock contract and sends it to the service (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-42).
  3. The service applies Same-day stock replacement: overwrite a matching record's quantity, otherwise create a new record using Manual stock-key allocation, then save (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:99-117).
  4. Only after the service call returns does the UI confirm that a shipment was added and clear inputs. The success text also appears for replacement; it does not imply quantities were added together (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:42-43; src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:189-195).

There is no separate shipment lifecycle, receiving approval, stock summation or event publication.

Workflow 4: Initial sample catalog provisioning and exposed maintenance operations

The first database initialization creates an absent database and seeds classifications, merchandise, dated inventory and historical promotions. This is a startup data-initialization path, not a scheduled promotion-refresh process (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:12-16; src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\CatalogDBInitializer.cs:11-20).

Item lookup/create/update/remove operations are exposed at the service but not connected to the active desktop controller. Create uses a max-ID allocation; update marks the provided entity modified; remove passes the provided entity to Remove. These are service capabilities, not user workflows demonstrated by the checked-in UI (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:33-44,65-82; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-157).

Cross-Service Data Flows

The only application network boundary is desktop → CatalogService. The desktop obtains products and promotions in separate calls and joins them by applying the same selected discount to every displayed product; this is client-side composition, not API-gateway or cross-microservice aggregation. Brands/types are fetched independently to populate choices. Stock enquiries and changes use item identifiers from the product selection (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-84,88-143).

No broker, choreography, distributed transaction, compensating workflow or circuit-breaker fallback exists in the active implementation. A missing promotion yields undiscounted prices; a missing stock row yields zero. Service unavailability is not mapped to either result because calls are not caught or retried (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-30,90-117; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-84).

The compiled mock is not wired into startup or hosting and cannot be treated as an offline fallback; its discount method throws. The service-side hand-written client and UWP-style desktop helper files are excluded from the respective explicit compile lists (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogServiceMock.cs:118-120; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc:1; src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj:79-94; src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:89-103,109-113,155-159).

Version & Compatibility Risks

The service targets .NET Framework 4.6.1 and the client 4.7; the 4.6.1 target is out of support, while 4.7 servicing depends on the deployed Windows lifecycle. EF6 6.1.3, Newtonsoft.Json 6.0.4 and WebApi.Client 5.2.3 are old pinned releases and warrant compatibility and advisory review before modernization. This document does not claim a live vulnerability scan or infer the installed runtime (src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj:15; src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:11; both packages.config files).

  • Both manifests label packages net461, although the desktop project targets v4.7; framework-target metadata differs from the project target (src\eShopWinForms\packages.config:3-5; src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj:11).
  • No package lockfile, central package file, test project or test-scoped package declaration was found in this scoped solution. Transitive edges cannot be reliably reconstructed from these declarations alone (eShopLegacyNTier.sln:6-9; both package manifests).

Entity Model

erDiagram %% All entities owned by eShopWCFService CatalogBrand ||--o{ CatalogItem : "classifies" CatalogType ||--o{ CatalogItem : "categorizes" CatalogItem ||--o{ CatalogItemsStock : "logical item reference only" CatalogBrand { int Id PK "application assigned" string Brand "maximum length 50; non Unicode" } CatalogType { int Id PK "application assigned" string Type "maximum length 50; non Unicode" } CatalogItem { int Id PK "application assigned" string Description string Name decimal Price "SQL money; configured precision 19 and scale 4" string Picturefilename int CatalogBrandId FK int CatalogTypeId FK } CatalogItemsStock { int StockId PK "application assigned" datetime Date "SQL date" int CatalogItemId "logical reference; no mapped navigation" int AvailableStock } DiscountItem { int Id PK "conventional generated key" double Size datetime Start "SQL date" datetime End "SQL date" }

CatalogItem has unidirectional, non-virtual CatalogBrand and CatalogType navigation properties and non-nullable foreign-key IDs. No inverse collection or explicit cascade policy is declared; normal EF conventions govern relationships. FindCatalogItem explicitly queries both classifications; the catalog list does not call Include or populate those navigations explicitly (src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItem.cs:27-35; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:33-62).

The stock-to-item line is a logical relationship inferred from queries, not evidence of an enforced EF/database foreign key: CatalogItemsStock contains only a scalar CatalogItemId and no navigation or fluent relationship configuration. No composite unique constraint for item/date, explicit index, row-version concurrency token or relationship to discounts is declared (src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItemsStock.cs:10-25; src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:24-40).

Entity sources and persistence constraints:

  • src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogBrand.cs:10-19 and Models\CatalogType.cs:10-19: keys are not database generated; classification strings have a length annotation of 50. Non-Unicode mapping is in src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:26-38.
  • src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItem.cs:10-35: item key is not database generated; price uses SQL money; precision is configured in src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:30-32. Strings other than classification labels have no declared length bounds.
  • src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItemsStock.cs:10-25: explicit table name, StockId key with no database generation, and date-only SQL column.
  • src\eShopWCFService\Models\DiscountItem.cs:11-31: integer key without DatabaseGenerated(None); fractional discount and inclusive date range are plain mutable persisted values.

Key Repository Methods

There are no repository interfaces or inherited repository CRUD abstractions. CatalogService operates directly on EntityModel sets.

No raw SQL, stored procedure, cross-service batch query or explicit TransactionScope is present in these methods. Each SaveChanges is its own EF persistence boundary; reads and preceding max-ID allocation are not enclosed in an application transaction. Context disposal is implemented by the service (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:65-117).

Caching Strategy

No distributed cache, MemoryCache, query cache, TTL, invalidation policy or EF second-level cache is configured in the inspected context/service/config (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:10-40; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-117; src\eShopWCFService\Web.config:52-64). EF change tracking and local ToList materialization are not a shared application cache. The unused CatalogServiceMock keeps lists in memory but is neither activated nor a production cache (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogServiceMock.cs:13-24; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc:1).

Data Ownership Boundaries

One service owns one database for all five model types; there are no database-per-microservice or schema-per-context boundaries. The desktop reads and writes through SOAP operations, never directly querying the database in its active path. Its controller combines catalog records with a separately returned discount for presentation, not cross-database joins (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-84; src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27).

Reads and writes share the same context/model; no CQRS read store, outbox, event replication or eventual-consistency mechanism is declared. Product image binaries reside in desktop assets, while the database stores a filename; deployed image-directory availability is a separate filesystem dependency (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:18-22; src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:55-61).
